title: The Pen Still Has Work
logline: A pen travels through two successful office automations and reveals, at the review desk, why a finished output still leaves a professional job to do.
angle_executed: In the KGS workflows described by AWS, the machine's finished output is still unfinished professional work.
vo_scope: Word budget only; no VO or storyboard written.
cold_open_first_3_seconds: Extreme macro: a cool steel output roller feeds a crisp REPORT into frame. A large oxblood pen slides alongside it, its cap skittering one inch farther than its barrel. The page says OUTPUT READY; the pen has made no mark. A swift pullback reveals a human hand reaching for the output. This is an illustrative office, not a claimed KGS interface.
dramatic_engine: The opposing force is an ambiguous finish line. The software can finish the job it was given while the person still has a different job. The film gives both jobs visible substance and lets neither erase the other.

hero.name: ReviewPen
hero.kind: Ordinary faceless pen, extracted from the shelf PenAndDocument, not a corporation or personified Native subject.

states.state: Capped and lying beside newly produced output; no mark made.
Parked horizontally above the DORA cutaway, acting as a fixed scale reference while records move.
Uncapped and resting diagonally beside separate first-draft sections.
Held for a small, neutral refinement mark in the draft. The mark is an edit, not a correction of a fabricated error.
Turned toward the DORA report for professional examination, then resting across the two separate task labels in the button.

hero.continuity_rule: Same silhouette and collar in every act, including a visible pen at each act boundary. Match cuts carry the pen between explanatory sets; they do not claim one actual procurement file passes through both tools.
hero.button_state: The pen rests above two separate finished outputs and points into the professional work area, still uncapped.

sets.name: Briefing wall
sets.physical_identity: Freestanding corporate nameplates, Alaska map with Kodiak marker, room-depth rails and the pen on a foreground ledge.

sets.name: DORA records room
sets.physical_identity: Tall receding filing cabinets, an email-input chute and a transparent records assembly table. Dark steel cabinets separate far/mid/near planes.

sets.name: Jumpstarter drafting studio
sets.physical_identity: Low wide document table, suspended input cards, separate page-section rails, warm angled task light and visible draft assembly space. No filing-cabinet backdrop.

sets.name: Professional review office
sets.physical_identity: A broad desk seen over the shoulder, document stand, task lamp and side return holding the alternate example. It is an office work surface, never a notebook.

treatment_scene_plan.action: Output arrives and the unmarked pen enters the same frame. Plant which finished job the page represents.
The camera passes Koniag's Kodiak connection to the KGS nameplate and September 11th announcement. The pen remains on the foreground ledge. No money arrows.
The Wingman announcement opens three physical labeled drawers: contracting, logistics and financial management. Then transition explicitly into earlier Army work.
An email-subject token labeled VENDOR IDENTIFIER enters. API routes retrieve SAM.gov records; only documented source names appear. The pen stays above the apparatus.
Prebuilt logic assembles records into a standardized report. It lands beside, rather than inside, the professional determination position. No LLM imagery or stopwatch.
A clearly separate Jumpstarter mechanism receives inputs; Bedrock/LLM section blocks become a FIRST DRAFT. Plant what the movable sections still need.

Give the automation its strongest fair case: inputs have become substantial, usable-looking output. Machine work visibly completes at REPORT ASSEMBLED and DRAFT GENERATED labels. The two examples are separate.

The professional reads and refines a draft section. The pen makes a neutral annotation; FIRST DRAFT remains visible. No wrong number, missing clause, rejection or measured delay. Secondary loop pays at 78 seconds.

Turn to the separate DORA example. The professional examines the assembled report for determination. Machine completion and professional action occupy different parts of the physical desk. Primary loop pays at 90 seconds.

Pull back to preserve both completed machine tasks and both remaining professional tasks. The pen bridges the spaces without issuing an award or signing a final contract. The angle resolves as a division of work.

Return to the fresh KGS announcement with the now-legible task boundaries. Reconfirm the corporate Alaska connection and briefly state that this announcement gives no contract value or quantified Alaska return.
Return to the opening roller and the same uncapped pen, now resting across the margins of the two illustrative output types. End on the question, then readable source and music credit treatment.

escalation: A page appears finished. The announced work expands from one office to three categories. A records mechanism proves it can assemble a report. A different mechanism generates a draft. The page becomes more sophisticated, and the professional's remaining job becomes more specific. The last act credits the prepared work before testing whether its status equals a completed decision.
earned_turn: At the review desk, the machine has succeeded at preparation. The person still examines a report and refines draft sections. The turn changes the meaning of finished without revealing a defect or withdrawing credit from the automation.

button.line: When the output is ready, which job is finished?
button.image: The opening roller remains behind two separate outputs labeled REPORT and FIRST DRAFT. The same oxblood pen rests in the professional work area, uncapped, with its silver collar catching the task light.
button.loop_back: The opening unmarked pen now has an intelligible role; the question tests task boundaries, not machine failure.

sight_gags.gag: The pen cap rolls a fraction farther than the heavy barrel and rocks to a stop. Pure desk physics; no delayed paperwork claim.
The financial-management drawer opens with such exact alignment that its loose generic divider tabs keep wiggling after the drawer stops. No institution or person is the joke.
A source-tab stack lands squarely, while one blank corner of the stack flutters a beat longer before settling. The report content is not wrong.
The FIRST DRAFT tag is oversized enough that a tiny generic binder jaw opens wide to hold it, then settles. The status is funny in scale, never mocked as a failure.

act3_test.name: The Completed Job
act3_test.strongest_fair_case_against_angle: The machine has produced exactly the preparation output requested. Calling it unfinished can unfairly make useful automation sound like a failed system.
act3_test.draw_at_full_strength: Show complete records assembled and a substantial draft generated. Nothing breaks, vanishes or receives a failure mark. Then change the inspection scale to the documented professional actions, reading for determination and refining sections. Both contributions survive in the final wide frame.
act3_test.resolution: The claim concerns whose job is complete. It does not deny the machine's completed preparation task or certify net productivity.
act3_test.nature_of_test: An explicit check of output status against the documented workflow, not a fabricated empirical performance trial.

primary_loop.promise: What is still unfinished when this output is ready? The pen is present but its professional role is not yet explained.
primary_loop.payoff: The separate DORA report is physically examined for determination; the finished machine output occupies a different stage from the person's job.

secondary_loop.promise: The generated first draft appears in independent sections. What happens to those sections after the machine stops?
secondary_loop.payoff: The professional refines a section, retaining FIRST DRAFT status. No invented error is necessary.

padding_test.why_90second_cut_worse: Without giving the machine a completed job, the film implies that human review proves automation did not work.
Without the specific edit, human review becomes a slogan and Jumpstarter's first-draft status has no visible consequence.
Without this separate task, the film merges DORA and Jumpstarter into one pipeline and makes two different outputs look interchangeable.
Without the synthesis view, the last action may overwrite the first in memory and the film loses its fair credit for useful preparation.

retention_plan.sag_prevention: At 69 seconds move from the entire drafting studio to over-shoulder work. At 79 seconds change both output type and professional verb. At 91 seconds reveal the whole division of work. No extended waiting or generic disclaimer cards.

small_story_driven_extension: Extract and generalize PenAndDocument's existing pen as a reusable ReviewPen with cap, held angle and neutral annotation-contact state. Reuse its shading and silhouette. This is a pen-work gap; the existing asset only hovers and trembles. No signature or approval behavior.
freshness_vs_last_two: September 11th followed FlightCrate over a missing road; September 12th centered a research notebook/Sheet with lilac, ivory and citron. This treatment uses an oxblood pen, steel-blue interiors, multiple workrooms, repeated scale changes and an office-output boundary. No notebook, crate, road or research task instrument is restaged.
palette: Oxford blue cabinets, cool steel, paper white, one oxblood pen, restrained warm desk light. Status ink remains neutral; no success-green or failure-red coding.
fact_and_visual_limits: Every earlier-work scene carries AWS CASE STUDY and EARLIER ARMY PROCUREMENT.
DORA retrieves through APIs and applies prebuilt logic; Jumpstarter generates first drafts.
Use only VENDOR IDENTIFIER, never a real or invented valid UEI.
All office sets are explanatory illustrations, not actual product UIs or physical hardware.
No stopwatch, portfolio totals, approval stamp, automatic award, failure incident or measured review wait.
No local return, hiring or benefit extrapolation.
Koniag and KGS remain named corporations; no cultural props, Native characterization or generic Tribal narrative.
Generic professional is not portrayed as a named source or an Alaska Native person.
